items: While Google Drive sync is on, your Google picture now sits at the top of the app on every screen, so you can always see which account is syncing. Tap it to open the sync settings.
Every attribute score now shows ▲/▼ against your last take on the same exercise.
The halves / thirds / quarters table now scores every attribute in each part — not just pace — with the change from the first part to the last, so you can see what held up and what faded.

Cowork Sync: replies from your AI coach now wait for you to review them (tick which exercises to keep) before anything changes, can be undone from the run history, and each channel can run on a schedule.
The app now starts in light or dark to match your device, until you pick a theme yourself.
Streaks and the activity calendar now go by your own local day, so late-evening practice counts for today.
Settings → Erase everything on this device removes all of SpeechImprover's data here, and leaves your Google Drive copy alone.
When Google Drive sync is on, Settings shows your Google picture and name.
Everything now loads from the app's own site: no outside font or code services.
New default font (Atkinson Hyperlegible), with a font choice under Settings → Theme.
Longer takes are split into halves, thirds or quarters, with a grade for how well you held your pace.
After each take: how it compares with your last try at the same exercise, your best on it, and today's streak.
After reading a passage, Drill the misses gives you a quick drill of the words you misread or skipped.
Press Space on the results screen to go again.
Just speak: one click (sidebar, dashboard or Ctrl-K) and you're recording free speech after a 3-2-1.
Voice Lab → Echo practice plays your voice back a moment late through headphones, to help you slow down and articulate.
Reading passages have a Listen first button that reads the text aloud with the current word underlined.
Free speaking has a talk-length picker, and the timer turns green, yellow and red like a speaking club's timing lights.
Results show how your pace changed over the take.
Hedging words like “I think”, “maybe” and “just” are marked in free-speech transcripts.
Reading passages show words correct per minute.
